newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda does not deny military foray into Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Uganda does not deny military foray into Zaire.

text.p: Ugandan officials said on Tuesday Ugandan troops shelled eastern Zaire but did not deny Kampala newspaper reports they had pushed into Zaire and since returned.

Foreign Ministry Spokesman Louis Balinda said Uganda denied accusations by Zaire's government that Ugandan troops fought alongside Zairean rebels to capture the eastern Zairean coffee-growing town of Beni.
But Balinda said Ugandan government forces shelled Zaire.
"Shells travel a distance of around a kilometre (half -a-mile). So from our border and pursuing rebels, the shells may have landed inside Zaire. That does not suggest that we invaded Zaire," he said.
Most shells cover considerably more than one kilometre.
The privately-owned Crusader newspaper said in a report from the Ugandan border town of Kasese that Ugandan civilians and soldiers had celebrated the overrunning of Zairean towns by Ugandan troops.
It quoted Ugandan Army Lieutenant-Colonel Geoffrey Muheesi as saying Ugandan soldiers crossed into Zaire only because they were attacked and "we had no alternative but...to pursue them".
Crusader said the Ugandan army had taken over the eastern Zairean towns of Masabwa, Kasindi, Manda and Mutaga and said excited Ugandan soldiers carried bottles of beer in Kasindi.
"We entered as if we were entering our homes," it quoted someone who followed the army into Zaire as saying. But it added that the soldiers had since returned to their posts in Uganda.

"If the Crusader spoke to villagers and location commanders, that's that," Balinda told Reuters. "I am not in a position to dispute or agree with the report. He said Kasese and other nearby border districts were calm but very tense on Tuesday.
Ugandan army officers would only also say all soldiers were at their positions inside Uganda.
The officers said residents of Ugandan areas bordering on Zaire, including a pygmy population in the vast Similiki national park, were being mobilised to repulse any external threat.

The Zaire government at the weekend accused Uganda of using tanks and armoured vehicles to capture the towns of Beni and Kasindi, just over 200 km (120 miles) from Goma city, one of three key eastern border settlements seized by Zairean rebels.
A Zairean military source said on Monday authorities were weighing how best to respond to the attacks by Ugandan troops.
But missionary sources said on Monday Beni had been captured by Zairean rebels.
Beni, so far the northernmost town lost by the Zaire army, is close to where the Ugandan troops have attacked Ugandan rebels based inside eastern Zaire over the past three weeks.
The independent Monitor newspaper said on Tuesday Ugandan troops had camped for a time inside Zaire after arriving in the Zairean town of Rume, 20 km (13 miles) from the Ugandan border.
It estimated 44 people -- 22 government soldiers and 22 Ugandan rebels -- were killed in fighting in Rume since Friday.
It said Ugandan troops had recovered a total of 40 weapons.

The newspaper quoted an army officer at the border post of Mpondwe as saying Ugandan soldiers destroyed Ugandan rebel camps in the Virunga and Kamirongo hills and "sent the rebels on the run inside Zaire". It added that five rebels had been captured.
Balinda said the Monitor report was exaggerated but did not give an official version of the casualty figures. "Our version of events is different. Our troops are at the border," he said.
